summary: This is a Snowflake SQL reference page for the DROP ROLE command, which removes a specified role from the system. It covers the syntax (DROP ROLE [IF EXISTS] <name>), identifier rules for double-quoted names, and usage notes on irrecoverability, future privileges requiring MANAGE GRANTS, automatic removal of grants, and revocation of role grants to users. It includes a query against snowflake.account_usage.grants_to_roles to find grants naming a role and a simple example.
one_line: Snowflake reference for the DROP ROLE command, which permanently removes a role and its grants from the account.
key_facts: DROP ROLE removes the specified role from the system.
The syntax is DROP ROLE [ IF EXISTS ] <name>.
If the role identifier contains spaces or special characters, the entire string must be enclosed in double quotes.
Identifiers enclosed in double quotes are case-sensitive.
Dropped roles cannot be recovered; they must be recreated.
If a role has a future privilege as a grantor or grantee, the role can only be dropped by a user with a role that has the MANAGE GRANTS privilege.
All current and future grants that name the role as either the grantor or the grantee are removed when the role is dropped.
To retrieve privilege grants naming a role as grantor or grantee, query snowflake.account_usage.grants_to_roles with WHERE grantee_name = upper('<role_name>') OR granted_by = upper('<role_name>').
If a role is a grantor of roles to users, dropping the role revokes these grants automatically.
The example DROP ROLE myrole; drops the role named myrole.
